design_note: The existing labs separate discovery and resource entitlement. This comparison adds credential audience separation across an MCP server and its backend, showing the precise rejection before a handler runs. The successful read still depends on independently enforced scope and resource checks.

source.title: Security Best Practices
source.concept: An MCP server must reject access tokens not issued for it. Passing an unvalidated client token through to another API bypasses the intended trust boundaries.
source.scope: The two fictional credential profiles and checkout read are constructed. Correct audience handling does not itself authorize a resource or establish result truth.

lesson.anchor: Enterprise patterns: registry, gateway, versioning and governance
lesson.title: One read crosses two credential boundaries
lesson.intro: AegisOps requests an authorized checkout latency read through obs-mcp. Compare two credential configurations for the same request; the backend is metrics-api.

data.input: One checkout read: host -> obs-mcp -> metrics-api.

left.title: Reuse backend token
steps: Host offers token with audience metrics-api
obs-mcp detects it was issued elsewhere
Reject before invoking the read handler
left.result: No read: a backend credential is not an MCP credential

right.title: Separate audiences
steps: Host offers valid token for obs-mcp
Backend checks principal, scope and service
right.result: Read proceeds only after both boundaries authorize it

read: The requested business operation is identical on both sides.
The left token is valid for a different service.
The right path obtains appropriate credentials and checks authority at each boundary.
lesson.question: Can changing the audience text locally repair the left credential?
lesson.answer: No. The issuer authenticates the token claims; editing the audience does not create an issuer-approved credential. Obtain the correct profile through the authorized identity flow. The MCP server and backend still enforce their own permissions.
lesson.takeaway: Credentials must be issued for the boundary that validates them.
lesson.assumption: Fictional profiles; both services enforce trusted identity, current scope and resource policy. Credentials stay outside model context.
